name: Residencia Temporal -- Remunerated Activities Subcategory

qualifying_event.description: A foreign national with a signed employment contract (notarized in Chile), a service contract exceeding 90 days, or a formal job offer from a Chilean employer applies for the Remunerated Activities subcategory of Residencia Temporal.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Employment contract signed at a Chilean notary, or a formal job offer from a Chilean employer.

requirements.blocker_text: Employment contract signed at a Chilean notary with an employer maintaining a Chilean office or branch.
requirements.fix_path: Secure employer sponsorship and notarize an employment contract in Chile.

requirements.blocker_text: Employer must demonstrate financial capacity via tax documentation or proof of economic solvency.
For employers with 25+ employees, foreign workers may not exceed 15% of the workforce (at least 85% must be Chilean nationals); no quota applies for employers with 25 or fewer employees.
Formal job offer from a Chilean employer; must present an executed employment contract within 45 days of arrival to convert to a 1-year permit.

evidence_required.document: Notarized employment contract or formal job offer

outcome.duration_length: contract route: up to 2 years, extendable for successive 2-year periods; job-offer route: initial 90 days, converts to 1 year on presenting an executed contract within 45 days of arrival

sources.title: serviciomigraciones.cl (SERMIG) -- Remunerated Activities subcategory: dependent employment, service contracts over 90 days, or formal job offers; contract route up to 2 years extendable; job-offer route 90 days converting to 1 year within a 45-day window; job loss doesn't automatically revoke the permit

mintrab.gob.cl (Chile's Ministry of Labour) -- hiring foreign workers: 15% foreign-worker cap for employers with 25+ employees (no cap below that), equal labour rights (minimum wage, hours, benefits, union participation) for foreign workers, 15-day employer notification requirement on contract termination

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Chile). Modeled PUBLISHED -- both requirement groups trace to tier-1 government sources (SERMIG and the Ministry of Labour). work_rights is 'restricted' since the contract route ties work to the sponsoring employer, though job loss does not automatically revoke the permit (per SERMIG), a more worker-favorable feature than most sponsored-work routes in this dataset. The 15% foreign-worker quota is a real, binding cap distinct from most countries modeled so far, disclosed explicitly as a hard requirement on the EMPLOYER side rather than the applicant.
